messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High - service-discovery.svc cluster reports elevated SRV lookup errors in us-west-2b. Alerting policy: srv_lookup_error_rate > 5% over 1m. Affected: internal API traffic and model-router in us-west-2b. Root TS: 1755678901

alice-ops: ACKed. I'm oncall for the hour, taking lead. Starting triage — tagging @raj-sre + @marta-infra.

raj-sre: on it. quick question: is this CONSUL or CoreDNS showing the errors? metrics look like 503s from coredns sidecar.

marta-infra: infra graphs show increased TCP RSTs from us-west-2b control plane to consul-leader-us-west-2a. Could be cross-AZ route flap.

kevin-platform: I see a spike in srv query latencies at the model-router: 95th went from 12ms -> 1.2s around 1755678840.

alice-ops: reproduction: `dig @10.0.10.12 _svc._tcp.service.consul SRV +short` from a node in us-west-2b times out intermittently.

alice-ops: running `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=coredns -o wide` shows some coredns pods on us-west-2b with `Ready 0/1`.

raj-sre: pulling logs from one failed coredns pod: ```
2025-09-02T14:08:12Z error: upstream lookup failed: context deadline exceeded
2025-09-02T14:08:13Z warn: connection reset by peer
```

marta-infra: checked VPC flow logs for us-west-2b -> us-west-2a on control plane subnets. There's an unusual route propagation event at 1755678800 where a peering route was withdrawn then re-added.

alice-ops: timeline: route withdrawal ~1755678800, SRV lookup latency spike ~1755678840, pager fire 1755678901. Looks correlated.

eve-support: any customer-facing impact yet? I can start drafting a status note.

kevin-platform: internal RPCs to service-discovery queuing - this would surface as 503s to customers using dedicated deployments in us-west-2b. We have a few active Dedicated clusters there.

alice-ops: initial impact: ~12% of internal SRV lookups failing for services in us-west-2b; retry logic reduces full outage but increases latency; customer-facing errors reported from 3 Dedicated customers. Escalating to SEs.

raj-sre: mitigation attempt 1: restart coredns pods in us-west-2b to clear stale connections to consul. `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/coredns -n kube-system --field-selector=spec.nodeName=us-west-2b-*` (executed).

incident-bot: Deploybot: Restart job queued by alice-ops. Job id: db-1755678940.

marta-infra: hold on — don't restart everything yet. If the route flap is ongoing, restarts will just reconnect to a flaky control plane. I recommend trying route/peering fix first and failover to us-west-2a for control plane traffic.

alice-ops: good call. rolling back recent peering change now. Peering change was a route propagation update from earlier maintenance. Initiating rollback with cloud CLI: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd --destination-cidr-block 10.1.0.0/16 --instance-id i-xxxx` (internal run).

marta-infra: route replacement accepted. Propagation timestamp ~1755679000. Confirming control plane connectivity to consul-leader from us-west-2b.

raj-sre: while propagation completes, enabling fallback: update service-discovery sidecar config to prefer consul proxies in us-west-2a for reads. Patch applied: `consul.config.read_preference=us-west-2a,us-west-2b` (hot patch).

kevin-platform: applied traffic split: 80% prefer local, 20% prefer us-west-2a for new SRV reads to avoid thundering herd.

alice-ops: monitoring: SRV error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% over the last 2m. Good sign.

eve-support: notifying affected customers: "We're seeing elevated service discovery failures in us-west-2b. We've put mitigations in place and expect degraded latency for the next hour. We'll update as we have more info." Sending now. :email:

incident-bot: Pager: on-call handoff ping — @alice-ops has been on-call for 22 minutes. No handoff requested.

marta-infra: peering rollback completed and route table stabilized; VPC flow logs now show normal ACKs. Looks like the root cause is propagation bug in the peering service during last maintenance window.

raj-sre: confirming consul metrics: RPC error rate down to baseline, consul leader elections unchanged. coredns readiness back to 1/1 for restarted pods.

kevin-platform: customer errors reported reduced to 0 in the last 5m. Removing immediate mitigations gradually.

alice-ops: final mitigation steps: 1) keep read_preference patch for 30m to smooth traffic, 2) monitor for 30m, 3) leave coredns pods restarted.

eve-support: update posted to status page: "Mitigation in place; service discovery errors reduced. Root cause: route propagation regression in peering change. Investigating permanent fix."

marta-infra: filing infra task to prevent future peering propagation race — internal ticket INFRA-3621. Also scheduling postmortem with networking team.

alice-ops: thanks team. I'll keep eyes for 30m and then clear the pager if stable. If anyone sees another spike, @alice-ops please DM.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Created incident report draft id ir-1755679100.

alice-ops: closing note: customer impact minimal due to retries but latency increased; three Dedicated customers had errors that auto-recovered. Postmortem will map timeline + permanent mitigations (stronger route prop validation + canary for peering changes). :white_check_mark:
